critical_code_review_comments: server.py upload_image: content type is trusted from the client Content-Type header (file.content_type). A malicious client could set image/png on a non-image payload and get it stored. Consider validating magic bytes (e.g. imghdr / Pillow) before persisting. Not blocking since ext is only used for the storage path suffix and serve_file returns the same declared content_type.

server.py serve_file: no auth or referer check — /api/files/<id> is fully public. This is intentional per spec ('files served publicly') but note that the uuid namespace is the only access control. Predictable enumeration is infeasible (uuid4) but audit logs are absent — consider a soft rate limit on GET /api/files/ if abuse is a concern.

server.py has no DELETE endpoint for uploaded files — Reset only clears the content_overrides key, leaving orphan blobs in Emergent storage. Test iteration created blobs that will accumulate over time. Consider a periodic sweeper or a DELETE /api/files/{id} admin endpoint that flips is_deleted and removes the object.

ContentEditor.jsx Field uploadImage: prefixes API + data.url without checking that data.url starts with '/'. Also no client-side MAX size guard — user can select a >5MB file and only see the toast after full network upload. A quick f.size > 5*1024*1024 check before FormData would improve UX.

ContentEditor.jsx: onDraft posts drafts for every keystroke including in rich (Quill) fields — for heavy pages the postMessage payload can rebuild the entire preview tree on every char. A small debounce (e.g. 150ms) around postDrafts would reduce iframe re-renders.

registry.js flattenSource: /(^|\.)(image|logo|src)$/ + extension check is fine, but the 'src' key also matches unrelated fields (e.g. any future data.src property). Consider a whitelist of explicit image roots (hero.image, growth.clients.*.logo, footer.badges.*) to avoid accidental exposure.
